agent_trace.summary: On brain MRI, infarction is suggested by focal parenchymal signal abnormality in a vascular territory, often affecting the cortical and/or subcortical gray-white junction and sometimes causing regional swelling. In the very early phase, diffusion restriction may be the most sensitive finding; over time, infarcts can evolve to encephalomalacia and volume loss. The retrieved examples only weakly indicate the possibility of infarct in the head/brain, so they are not specific to this anatomy but are consistent with the general idea that infarction can be present on imaging.

key_facts: Acute infarcts often show restricted diffusion on DWI with low ADC values.
Cortical and subcortical involvement in a vascular distribution is a common pattern of ischemic injury.
Chronic infarcts may appear as tissue loss, gliosis, and ex-vacuo enlargement of adjacent CSF spaces.
Mass effect, sulcal effacement, or loss of gray-white differentiation can occur in more acute infarction.
